scope: Uncommitted root Android startup permission fix and installed CallKeep facade regression suite; no application-source edits by this reviewer.
conclusion: No remaining blocking finding in the reviewed passive-registration change. Emulator and physical-device acceptance remain separate.

findings.issue: Android setup prompts during passive session hydration
evidence: CallKeep index.js _setupAndroid calls checkPhoneAccountPermission and may open phone-account settings.
RNCallKeepModule.registerPhoneAccount stores settings and registers Telecom account without invoking the permission request path.
registerEvents sets hasListeners, invokes startObserving and attaches the PhoneAccountHandle.
VoiceConnectionService.setAvailable(true) also sets initialized, preserving the required terminal setup state.

findings.issue: Android cold queued actions could be drained before the initial-events read
findings.status: resolved in source after independent review finding
evidence: Native startObserving copies and clears delayedEvents and emits RNCallKeepDidLoadWithEvents. This behavior also applied to the previous setup() path.
Service now attaches didLoadWithEvents before native registration on Android and iOS; didActivateAudioSession remains iOS-only.
Regression models registration-time drained events and an empty getInitialEvents cache: answer(A), end(A), answer(B) yields end(A), answer(B) once after owner hydration.

findings.issue: Registration does not establish permission or enabled phone account
evidence: Native hasPhoneAccount checks ConnectionService, required permissions, existing PhoneAccount and isEnabled without requesting access.
prepareForIncomingCall returns false on unavailable or errored account check.
callBackgroundTask revalidates current recipient/call and uses its notification fallback when native preparation is false.
Previously enabled accounts remain eligible without prompting.

verification.scope: Actual installed JavaScript facade with mocked native bridge; Java behavior separately inspected.
additionalChecks: Android concurrent setup registers once and never invokes setup/permission/settings/alert paths.
Failed registration clears partial listeners and retries without prompts.
iOS retains setup and four listeners.

limitations: This local review does not execute Java, Telecom, APNs, FCM, CallKit or a physical phone; full-app emulator rerun and physical-device call acceptance remain separate.

New Android installs intentionally remain on notification/in-app calling until the user grants phone permissions and enables the managed phone account. No new unsolicited permissions/settings flow is included.

CallContext explicitly requests RECORD_AUDIO and optionally CAMERA after call initiation/answer, before call RPC/provider creation; it does not request CallKeep phone permissions or enable the Telecom account.
The fallback still depends on available notification permissions and current authenticated call eligibility.
No backend mutation, native account activation, external delivery or deployment was performed by this review.
